# On Board Air compressor installation

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Install an on board air compressor by mounting it and connecting its feed lines. [t440]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the front plastic grill by carefully taking out four plastic clips.
2. [Partial] Locate a structural plate on the inside of the SW bumper to use as a mounting spot.
3. [Partial] Drill four holes that line up with the base plate holes of the compressor, removing rubber feet from those spots first.
4. [Partial] Mark and drill additional holes for air feed lines if not already done.
5. Tap one hole specifically for a 1/4" brass air nipple (threads measure like 5/8").
6. [Partial] Remove the quick disconnect fitting that came with the compressor to fit it into the tapped hole.
7. Install the compressor using your favorite fastener and secure it in place.
8. [Partial] Purchase three items: a 1/4" brass nipple, a 1/4" brass elbow, and an airline line with 1/4" brass fittings on both ends (Teflon stainless steel braided is suggested).
9. [Partial] Apply Teflon tape to the fitting connections.
10. Install the quick disconnect male fitting using a washer and a 1/4" brass coupler for easy disconnection later.
11. [Partial] Connect the other end of the airline hose to another quick disconnect male fitting on the back side of the first one.
12. Wire the compressor directly to the battery, utilizing its inline fuse in the power wire.
13. Access the square holes in the bumper to switch the unit on and off.

_Procedure reported by [t440]._

## Tools

- Drill [t440]
- Taps (for 1/4" brass nipple) [t440]
- Washer [t440]
- Brass coupler [t440]

## Parts

- [Partial] 3x 1/4" Brass fittings, nipple, elbow [t440]

- Portable compressor: e.g., Tsunami brand [t440]

## Tips & gotchas

- Remove rubber feet from the bumper before drilling. [t440]
- [Partial] Ensure compressor isn't too close to wires or hoses to prevent rubbing. [t440]
